arms.swarmos: SWARMOS product policy (graded ladder + Simplex kernel + perception fallback)
arms.swarmos_mhb_sep: SWARMOS + mutual-hold break + separating-motion exemption (kernel change, under evaluation)

command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 tools/run_experiment.py --name long_run_safety --scenarios rush_50 narrow_aisle_deadlock blocked_aisle --arms swarmos swarmos_mhb_sep --ticks 9000 --workers 4
name: long_run_safety

blocked_aisle.description: A busy run where a central aisle segment is sealed at t=20 s and reopened at t=80 s, invalidating in-flight reservations and forcing a fleet-wide reroute.
blocked_aisle.name: blocked_aisle
blocked_aisle.proves: Reservation invalidation, replanning under a changed map, and that the safety invariant counter stays at zero through the disruption.
blocked_aisle.title: Aisle blocked mid-run

narrow_aisle_deadlock.description: Cross aisles removed so every aisle is a single-file corridor with only two exits. Robots are forced into head-on and swap conflicts that a naive first-come planner deadlocks on.
narrow_aisle_deadlock.name: narrow_aisle_deadlock
narrow_aisle_deadlock.proves: Deadlock detection and the graded verdict ladder, plus deterministic lock arbitration when two robots claim the same cell on the same tick.
narrow_aisle_deadlock.title: Narrow aisle deadlock

rush_50.description: Fifty heterogeneous robots on the full floor with a 30-task opening burst and a sustained 1.5 tasks/s arrival rate. This is the default state the demo opens in.
rush_50.name: rush_50
rush_50.proves: Sustained 10 Hz coordination at fleet scale, zero collisions, and the throughput lead over the stop-and-wait baseline.
rush_50.title: Rush hour, 50 robots
